Poisoned

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
A surge in food poisonings amongst children assumed to be as a result of fake foods but could it be something else?

Summary:
Poisoning of children after exposure to pesticides is a major public health concern, particularly in countries with poorer urban populations, such as South Africa. This may stem from the illegal distribution and domestic use of street pesticides, which are highly hazardous agricultural pesticides -
Child and adolescent mortality associated with pesticide toxicity in Cape Town, South Africa, 2010–2019: a retrospective case review

Pesticide poisoning is a global health concern with approximately three million cases being reported on an annual basis. The latter includes both intentional and unintentional poisonings. Organophosphorus and carbamate insecticides are frequently found to be ‘responsible’ for pesticide poisoning in developing countries. In South Africa, aldicarb is the most potent carbamate pesticide and is sold in the informal markets as Temik.

This publicly available list of Highly Hazardous Pesticides, hitherto shrouded in secrecy and closely guarded by the pesticide industry, and using the categorisation and criteria developed by the FAO/WHO Joint Meeting on Pesticide Management, shows that there are 192 highly hazardous pesticides (HHPs) registered and in use in SA. Of this, only 16 have partial bans or restrictions.



Further information:
The recent suspected poisoning of six children in Naledi highlights the alarming rise in child fatalities linked to food poisoning. This troubling trend recalls last year's tragic deaths of two children, Neo Khang and Leon Jele, in the same community, and Refiloe Usman, 6, from Tsakane died after eating biscuits bought from a spaza shop while Lufuno Musa Bokang, 5, and Dimakatso Tsotsotso, 3, of Vosloorus died after eating chips. The growing number of incidents shows the problem is bigger than one could possibly imagine.

https://www.ewn.co.za/2024/10/10/naledi-children-deaths-spaza-shop-owner-s-partner-rubbishes-claims-snacks-were-poisoned

The culprits ? The government has pinned the blame on foreign run Spaza shops, they have been accused of unsanitary practices such a as sleeping in their shops, keeping pets, lack of pest control and the use of dangerous pesticides to eliminate rats and rodents. The number of inspections conducted across the country has risen considerably the City of Johannesburg alone boasting 4149 inspections conducted between July 2023 and June 2024 this amid uproars from political parties and fed up local communities, with Minister Ntshaveni urging South Africans to stop purchasing from unregistered spaza shops but is there even any evidence linking the 2?

https://www.news24.com/news24/politics/government/we-cannot-have-our-cake-and-eat-it-dont-buy-from-unregistered-spaza-shops-ntshavheni-says-20241010

https://www.iol.co.za/sundayindependent/news/poisonous-food-warning-for-gauteng-parents-children-936e1f66-731e-40a3-9918-a1c1dc8b3882#google_vignette

In 2021, two families in the Eastern Cape were devastated by the sudden loss of their children: Sinothando Gwendu, aged 11; Olwam Gwendu, aged 7; and 4-month-old Athenkosi Gwendu died shortly after consuming instant noodles. Similarly, in Mpumalanga, 9-year-old Thato Makofane and her older brother, Keamogetswe Makofane 13, faced a comparable fate.

Toxicologist Dr Gerhard Verdoorn worked with the manufacturer in the Eastern Cape and helped prove they were being falsely accused by the DOH , the packs were found to have been tampered with and contained the deadly pesticide. Dr Verdoorn explains that the ease and cost that comes with purchasing these dangerous chemicals is what exacerbates the situation. Packets of the poisons can be found at street corners, taxi ranks sometimes even displayed together with food items starting from as little as R5.

The Buffalo City Metro municipal preliminary report noted an investigation in Mdantsane where Aldicarb banned in 2016 due to its highly acute toxicity is in open circulation for rodent control and the city of Joburg and the Director of Environmental Health in Ekurhuleni Dr Jerry Chaka confirmed the presence of organophosphate a toxic chemical found in rat poison when autopsies were conducted on the children.

Dangerous poisons like Aldicarb, Terbufos, Methamidophos, and Diazinon are available from street vendors, often in small clear packets or liquid bottles and even Facebook Marketplace. Aldicarb, in particular, is popular, despite buyers often being unaware that a mere match head's worth can kill an adult in just 20 minutes. Aldicarb has only one official distributor in South Africa, which implements strict distribution measures. This distributor has added Bitrex to their product to make it detectable and included a vomiting-inducing drug to mitigate poisoning effects if ingested. Despite these measures, the illegal street version of Aldicarb mostly hails from China and a generic version manufactured in Zimbabwe.

Dr Verdoorn who has been investigating these cases for years says that most aldicarb is smuggled from Zimbabwe through our porous boarders one can easily cross the border on foot with a load of aldicarb and go unnoticed. It is also shipped in from China hidden in shipments and is then distributed nationally. It is an extremely organised crime syndicate, on one particular case when they tried to trace the addresses and names discovered on confiscated shipments all were fake and led to dead ends.

Poisoned Script - 07/11/2024

Intro sequence


FADE TO BLACK


VO 1 Across the country, a dark mystery circulates township communities… its victims: children.

VO 2: In October last year, at least eight children died in the Free State and Gauteng after eating snacks bought from local spaza shops.

VO 3: Communities took to the streets, looting the foreign owned spaza shops that they blamed for the deaths of their children.

VO4: Local municipalities responded with raids on spaza shops, targeting expired and fake foods, and undocumented foreign nationals.

VO5: But by December, municipalities shifted focus and the children’s deaths don't appear to have been properly investigated .

VO 6: Then… this year, more children died in Gauteng…

VO 7: In April, a young boy became violently ill and passed away in Vosloorus. Six months later, six children lost their lives in Naledi, Soweto.

VO 8: Government took notice.
UPSOUND: Ladies and gentlemen we are here today to inform you of the findings of our toxicologist the results show that the cause of death is unequivocally Terbufos, —-all the six children died of Terbufos ingestion.

VO 9: But could these deaths have been prevented?

FADE TO BLACK

@02:10 Nomazizi Ngwendu
…Sinothando - she was a well mannered child, who loved people and was a free spirit.
When it was time for our evening prayer she was the one who reminded me that: ‘Ma, it’s time to pray’.
VO 10: Nomazizi Ngwendu and her daughter Nomazandile live in Motherwell, Gqeberha, in the Eastern Cape. For three years, they’ve been mourning the sudden deaths of Nomazandile’s two daughters and her niece.
VO 11: In November 2021, Nomazizi returned home from running an errand. Eleven year-old Sinothando was cooking two-minute noodles, bought at the local spaza shop, for herself and her cousins.
UPSOUND - @07:59 Nomazizi Ngwendu - Sinothando said she had a stomach ache.
UPSOUND 09:07 Nomazizi - she started foaming at the mouth.
VO 10: As they rushed Sinothando to the hospital, the other two children fell ill as well. One of them was just a baby.
When I looked at her she was slowly dying. I said to my sister: ‘I feel helpless’.
VO 11: Two hours later, all three children were dead….

UPSOUND Nomazizi 17:03 -
What I can say is I was not ok after that. I asked God why He took the children... (crying)
VO 12: Weeks later, investigators established that the highly poisonous agricultural pesticide - Terbufos - was responsible for the children’s deaths. But the manufacturers of the noodles were cleared of any wrongdoing.

UPSOUND: it might be used by somebody who wants to murder somebody, it happens very often.

VO 14: Toxicologist, Dr Gerhard Verdoorn, runs the Griffin Poison Centre and works for CropLife - an organization which represents pesticide manufacturers. He assisted with the investigation into these three children’s deaths - and says Terbufos is all too common in these cases.

UPSOUND: 39:21 VERDOORN - It's been there for I would say about eight or nine years that we saw terbufos poisonings.

UPSOUND Masa: What's terbufos, Dr. Verdoorn?

UPSOUND VERDOORN : It's a granular organophosphate which is used for things like potatoes and maize to control nematodes and to control beetles and wireworms.

VO 15: Terbufos is a pesticide that can only legally be used in agriculture. But Dr Verdoorn says criminal syndicates often steal it from farms and sell it in smaller quantities in low-income areas, where it’s a popular - and quick - solution to rat infestations.

And from there, whether by accident or intent, it makes its way into popular foods.

UPSOUND
@ 6:58 Gerhard Verdoorn
…those foodstuffs are sold in exceptionally unhygienic shops with no control between what is foodstuff, what is the clothing and what are the pesticides. It's all one big dimmer car spool and there's a very good chance of contamination.Now we've got a national crisis.

PAUSE
DAN - map / treatment to take us from Motherwell, GQ to Tladi, Soweto

VO 19: But Terbufos is not the only hazardous pesticide readily available in these low income communities.

VO 20: In Tladi, Soweto - Tshepo Williams knows all too well how deadly the banned chemical aldicarb can be. Last year, his grandson Leon Jele collapsed on the street, minutes after eating snacks from a nearby spaza shop…

UPSOUND A040C028 Tshepo Williams - So he was laying here and the two sisters were with him here trying to resuscitate him.


VO 21: Leon later died, and Tshepo stated that the autopsy identified aldicarb—a banned pesticide known as two-step or halephirimi, meaning "you will not see the sunset"—as the cause. It's a popular rat poison,


Tshepo says, police still have not provided the official toxicology report.


UPSOUND Tshepo - I'm saying that this case is so cold, it's like we've buried that dog...let it be


UPSOUND MASA 01:01- So this spot here I'm sure you never want to be here?


UPSOUND Tshepo - But I have to pass here every time to pass here I will have to...I have no choice you see...from whichever direction you'll see this place…
EDIT NOTE - let him cry

VO 23: In October our producers went undercover in Soweto, in search of poisons sold on the street.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER Viz: Google Drive - Kliptown
00:53
R 10 ..R 5 …that one is place in the ceiling..even outside you can use it but most people use it in the ceilings ..it doesn’t smell

VO 24: In the Kliptown and Dobsonville taxi ranks, the problem became clear - several street vendors had what looked like rat poison on display - unmarked, and with no warning labels …

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER
03:20
Where do you stock these things?
03:45
At noord (taxi rank)
Producer: At Noord, is there a person you buy from specifically
03:57
Jahh just check at Noord

VO 24A: Our producers bought some samples of the rat poisons sold, and sent them to a lab for testing.

UPSOUND VERDOORN
@8:14 - I can tell you in the last two to three years with all my walkabouts in my area which is Gqeberha and Karega and even going to places in Pretoria and going into East London and so on. I have not seen a street vendor selling legal pesticides. Never.

VO 25: In his study, Verdoorn shows me some samples of highly poisonous pesticides sold on the street.

UPSOUND So I first want you to put on a glove. To safety first. Safety first, safety when you work with chemicals, even if I work with the most benign of chemicals,

Aldricarb, which has been completely banned in South Africa since 2016, is one of the deadliest… but it’s still readily available from street vendors.

A036C026
04:52
Look at this …
This is the little sachet with about 20 packets of nearly 5 grams each of Aldicarb. That they sell for R 20.

5:08
That's sufficient to kill 200 men in half an hour if you put it into the food.

VO 34: So who is supplying these illegal pesticides to these street vendors?

VO 35: Our team followed a lead to a well known mall in Johannesburg. It’s notorious for the sale of pesticides.

Viz: Google Drive: Joburg Mall video (please show their faces)
Producer: we want to buy in bulk ….
Shop owner: we don’t sell in bulk …no you’re not going to get it…nobody is going to give you

10:00
I know the supplier but I won’t give you
Producer: please, please
10:27
Which place exactly are you from?
Butterworth
10:35
You’re not the feds

VO 34: The lead went cold

PAUSE/TRANSITION

VO 26: According to Anna Shevel from nonprofit organisation Unpoison, legal, regulated, pesticides like Terbufos are more accessible than banned ones. . Unpoison is advocating for a complete ban on Terbufos in South Africa.

@11:09:20:17 - 11:09:34:24 ANNA SHEVEL
In recent studies of 2019 and all the recent data. Terbufos is the main culprit. For street poison, for pesticide, poisoning, in the townships.

UPSOUND: @ 11:10:42:48 - 11:11:06:35 Anna Shevel, Unpoison - It has been banned in Europe since 2014.

UPSOUND: So why are we legally using one of the most acutely toxic pesticides on our food?

VO 26: She says our legislation is not in line with global standards designed to keep the public safe.

UPSOUND @ 11:45:41:14 - 11:45:53:44 Anna - And there's a lot of vagueness and loopholes and inconsistencies in the current regulations that need to be addressed.

VO 27: The department of agriculture oversees the manufacture and distribution of pesticides. They have an inspectorate tasked with the enforcement of pesticide laws, but it lacks manpower

UPSOUND @11:38:39:28 - 11:39:12:36 - Anna Shevel, Unpoison
I know that there are very few compliance officers. I believe there is only one compliance officer in the whole of the Western Cape…this is woefully inadequate.

MASA transition
VO 36: But after the latest series of deaths, the department unleashed 80 health inspectors on Soweto this October to identify the chemical that had killed six children in Naledi.
A week later we visited the area to see if hazardous chemicals were still on sale…
UPSOUND A040C127

VO 37: Anyone selling pesticides requires a license from the department of health - these traders should be regularly inspected - but for decades they've been left unchecked

VO 38:Remember the poison we sent off to get tested? Well the results are in and it’s reason for concern - three of the four samples tested positive for terbufos
Dramatic music…show the test results..zoom in on terbufos and the peak on the graphs


@41:01 Gerhard Verdoorn
And to this date we've got no conclusion on what happened with the children in Gqeberha. Because we don't know whether the food was deliberately spiked in the spaza shop

VO 38: Meanwhile in the Eastern Cape,no arrests have been made relating to the deaths of the three Ngwendu children…

VO 39: The police say the Ngwendu investigation is still underway.
The department of agriculture passed the buck saying that all queries related to the poisoning of children have been centralized with the department of health. The Department of Health said none of its officials were willing to take part in an interview.

UPSOUND 11:32:49:08 - 11:33:07:00 Anna Shevel - Government departments,are all complicit in the failure of protecting public health.

VO: But for grieving families serious questions remain…

END

Carte Blanche HD mihle@combinedartists.co.za 10 November 2024 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: Poisoned Script - 07/11/2024 Intro sequence FADE TO BLACK VO 1 Across the country, a dark mystery circulates township communities… its victims: children. VO 2: In October last year, at least eight children died in the Free State and Gauteng after eating snacks bought from local spaza shops. VO 3: Communities took to the streets, looting the foreign owned spaza shops that they blamed for the deaths of their children. VO4: Local municipalities responded with raids on spaza shops, targeting expired and fake foods, and undocumented foreign nationals. VO5: But by December, municipalities shifted focus and the children’s deaths don't appear to have been properly investigated . VO 6: Then… this year, more children died in Gauteng… VO 7: In April, a young boy became violently ill and passed away in Vosloorus. Six months later, six children lost their lives in Naledi, Soweto. VO 8: Government took notice. UPSOUND: Ladies and gentlemen we are here today to inform you of the findings of our toxicologist the results show that the cause of death is unequivocally Terbufos, —-all the six children died of Terbufos ingestion. VO 9: But could these deaths have been prevented? FADE TO BLACK @02:10 Nomazizi Ngwendu …Sinothando - she was a well mannered child, who loved people and was a free spirit. When it was time for our evening prayer she was the one who reminded me that: ‘Ma, it’s time to pray’. VO 10: Nomazizi Ngwendu and her daughter Nomazandile live in Motherwell, Gqeberha, in the Eastern Cape. For three years, they’ve been mourning the sudden deaths of Nomazandile’s two daughters and her niece. VO 11: In November 2021, Nomazizi returned home from running an errand. Eleven year-old Sinothando was cooking two-minute noodles, bought at the local spaza shop, for herself and her cousins. UPSOUND - @07:59 Nomazizi Ngwendu - Sinothando said she had a stomach ache. UPSOUND 09:07 Nomazizi - she started foaming at the mouth. VO 10: As they rushed Sinothando to the hospital, the other two children fell ill as well. One of them was just a baby. When I looked at her she was slowly dying. I said to my sister: ‘I feel helpless’. VO 11: Two hours later, all three children were dead…. UPSOUND Nomazizi 17:03 - What I can say is I was not ok after that. I asked God why He took the children... (crying) VO 12: Weeks later, investigators established that the highly poisonous agricultural pesticide - Terbufos - was responsible for the children’s deaths. But the manufacturers of the noodles were cleared of any wrongdoing. UPSOUND: it might be used by somebody who wants to murder somebody, it happens very often. VO 14: Toxicologist, Dr Gerhard Verdoorn, runs the Griffin Poison Centre and works for CropLife - an organization which represents pesticide manufacturers. He assisted with the investigation into these three children’s deaths - and says Terbufos is all too common in these cases. UPSOUND: 39:21 VERDOORN - It's been there for I would say about eight or nine years that we saw terbufos poisonings. UPSOUND Masa: What's terbufos, Dr. Verdoorn? UPSOUND VERDOORN : It's a granular organophosphate which is used for things like potatoes and maize to control nematodes and to control beetles and wireworms. VO 15: Terbufos is a pesticide that can only legally be used in agriculture. But Dr Verdoorn says criminal syndicates often steal it from farms and sell it in smaller quantities in low-income areas, where it’s a popular - and quick - solution to rat infestations. And from there, whether by accident or intent, it makes its way into popular foods. UPSOUND @ 6:58 Gerhard Verdoorn …those foodstuffs are sold in exceptionally unhygienic shops with no control between what is foodstuff, what is the clothing and what are the pesticides. It's all one big dimmer car spool and there's a very good chance of contamination.Now we've got a national crisis. PAUSE DAN - map / treatment to take us from Motherwell, GQ to Tladi, Soweto VO 19: But Terbufos is not the only hazardous pesticide readily available in these low income communities. VO 20: In Tladi, Soweto - Tshepo Williams knows all too well how deadly the banned chemical aldicarb can be. Last year, his grandson Leon Jele collapsed on the street, minutes after eating snacks from a nearby spaza shop… UPSOUND A040C028 Tshepo Williams - So he was laying here and the two sisters were with him here trying to resuscitate him. VO 21: Leon later died, and Tshepo stated that the autopsy identified aldicarb—a banned pesticide known as two-step or halephirimi, meaning "you will not see the sunset"—as the cause. It's a popular rat poison, Tshepo says, police still have not provided the official toxicology report. UPSOUND Tshepo - I'm saying that this case is so cold, it's like we've buried that dog...let it be UPSOUND MASA 01:01- So this spot here I'm sure you never want to be here? UPSOUND Tshepo - But I have to pass here every time to pass here I will have to...I have no choice you see...from whichever direction you'll see this place… EDIT NOTE - let him cry VO 23: In October our producers went undercover in Soweto, in search of poisons sold on the street. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER Viz: Google Drive - Kliptown 00:53 R 10 ..R 5 …that one is place in the ceiling..even outside you can use it but most people use it in the ceilings ..it doesn’t smell VO 24: In the Kliptown and Dobsonville taxi ranks, the problem became clear - several street vendors had what looked like rat poison on display - unmarked, and with no warning labels … UPSOUND UNDERCOVER 03:20 Where do you stock these things? 03:45 At noord (taxi rank) Producer: At Noord, is there a person you buy from specifically 03:57 Jahh just check at Noord VO 24A: Our producers bought some samples of the rat poisons sold, and sent them to a lab for testing. UPSOUND VERDOORN @8:14 - I can tell you in the last two to three years with all my walkabouts in my area which is Gqeberha and Karega and even going to places in Pretoria and going into East London and so on. I have not seen a street vendor selling legal pesticides. Never. VO 25: In his study, Verdoorn shows me some samples of highly poisonous pesticides sold on the street. UPSOUND So I first want you to put on a glove. To safety first. Safety first, safety when you work with chemicals, even if I work with the most benign of chemicals, Aldricarb, which has been completely banned in South Africa since 2016, is one of the deadliest… but it’s still readily available from street vendors. A036C026 04:52 Look at this … This is the little sachet with about 20 packets of nearly 5 grams each of Aldicarb. That they sell for R 20. 5:08 That's sufficient to kill 200 men in half an hour if you put it into the food. VO 34: So who is supplying these illegal pesticides to these street vendors? VO 35: Our team followed a lead to a well known mall in Johannesburg. It’s notorious for the sale of pesticides. Viz: Google Drive: Joburg Mall video (please show their faces) Producer: we want to buy in bulk …. Shop owner: we don’t sell in bulk …no you’re not going to get it…nobody is going to give you 10:00 I know the supplier but I won’t give you Producer: please, please 10:27 Which place exactly are you from? Butterworth 10:35 You’re not the feds VO 34: The lead went cold PAUSE/TRANSITION VO 26: According to Anna Shevel from nonprofit organisation Unpoison, legal, regulated, pesticides like Terbufos are more accessible than banned ones. . Unpoison is advocating for a complete ban on Terbufos in South Africa. @11:09:20:17 - 11:09:34:24 ANNA SHEVEL In recent studies of 2019 and all the recent data. Terbufos is the main culprit. For street poison, for pesticide, poisoning, in the townships. UPSOUND: @ 11:10:42:48 - 11:11:06:35 Anna Shevel, Unpoison - It has been banned in Europe since 2014. UPSOUND: So why are we legally using one of the most acutely toxic pesticides on our food? VO 26: She says our legislation is not in line with global standards designed to keep the public safe. UPSOUND @ 11:45:41:14 - 11:45:53:44 Anna - And there's a lot of vagueness and loopholes and inconsistencies in the current regulations that need to be addressed. metadata.Unique Selling Point: A surge in food poisonings amongst children assumed to be as a result of fake foods but could it be something else?
metadata.Summary: Poisoning of children after exposure to pesticides is a major public health concern, particularly in countries with poorer urban populations, such as South Africa. This may stem from the illegal distribution and domestic use of street pesticides, which are highly hazardous agricultural pesticides - Child and adolescent mortality associated with pesticide toxicity in Cape Town, South Africa, 2010–2019: a retrospective case review Pesticide poisoning is a global health concern with approximately three million cases being reported on an annual basis. The latter includes both intentional and unintentional poisonings. Organophosphorus and carbamate insecticides are frequently found to be ‘responsible’ for pesticide poisoning in developing countries. In South Africa, aldicarb is the most potent carbamate pesticide and is sold in the informal markets as Temik. This publicly available list of Highly Hazardous Pesticides, hitherto shrouded in secrecy and closely guarded by the pesticide industry, and using the categorisation and criteria developed by the FAO/WHO Joint Meeting on Pesticide Management, shows that there are 192 highly hazardous pesticides (HHPs) registered and in use in SA. Of this, only 16 have partial bans or restrictions.
metadata.Further information: The recent suspected poisoning of six children in Naledi highlights the alarming rise in child fatalities linked to food poisoning. This troubling trend recalls last year's tragic deaths of two children, Neo Khang and Leon Jele, in the same community, and Refiloe Usman, 6, from Tsakane died after eating biscuits bought from a spaza shop while Lufuno Musa Bokang, 5, and Dimakatso Tsotsotso, 3, of Vosloorus died after eating chips. The growing number of incidents shows the problem is bigger than one could possibly imagine. https://www.ewn.co.za/2024/10/10/naledi-children-deaths-spaza-shop-owner-s-partner-rubbishes-claims-snacks-were-poisoned The culprits ? The government has pinned the blame on foreign run Spaza shops, they have been accused of unsanitary practices such a as sleeping in their shops, keeping pets, lack of pest control and the use of dangerous pesticides to eliminate rats and rodents. The number of inspections conducted across the country has risen considerably the City of Johannesburg alone boasting 4149 inspections conducted between July 2023 and June 2024 this amid uproars from political parties and fed up local communities, with Minister Ntshaveni urging South Africans to stop purchasing from unregistered spaza shops but is there even any evidence linking the 2? https://www.news24.com/news24/politics/government/we-cannot-have-our-cake-and-eat-it-dont-buy-from-unregistered-spaza-shops-ntshavheni-says-20241010 https://www.iol.co.za/sundayindependent/news/poisonous-food-warning-for-gauteng-parents-children-936e1f66-731e-40a3-9918-a1c1dc8b3882#google_vignette In 2021, two families in the Eastern Cape were devastated by the sudden loss of their children: Sinothando Gwendu, aged 11; Olwam Gwendu, aged 7; and 4-month-old Athenkosi Gwendu died shortly after consuming instant noodles. Similarly, in Mpumalanga, 9-year-old Thato Makofane and her older brother, Keamogetswe Makofane 13, faced a comparable fate. Toxicologist Dr Gerhard Verdoorn worked with the manufacturer in the Eastern Cape and helped prove they were being falsely accused by the DOH , the packs were found to have been tampered with and contained the deadly pesticide. Dr Verdoorn explains that the ease and cost that comes with purchasing these dangerous chemicals is what exacerbates the situation. Packets of the poisons can be found at street corners, taxi ranks sometimes even displayed together with food items starting from as little as R5. The Buffalo City Metro municipal preliminary report noted an investigation in Mdantsane where Aldicarb banned in 2016 due to its highly acute toxicity is in open circulation for rodent control and the city of Joburg and the Director of Environmental Health in Ekurhuleni Dr Jerry Chaka confirmed the presence of organophosphate a toxic chemical found in rat poison when autopsies were conducted on the children. Dangerous poisons like Aldicarb, Terbufos, Methamidophos, and Diazinon are available from street vendors, often in small clear packets or liquid bottles and even Facebook Marketplace. Aldicarb, in particular, is popular, despite buyers often being unaware that a mere match head's worth can kill an adult in just 20 minutes. Aldicarb has only one official distributor in South Africa, which implements strict distribution measures. This distributor has added Bitrex to their product to make it detectable and included a vomiting-inducing drug to mitigate poisoning effects if ingested. Despite these measures, the illegal street version of Aldicarb mostly hails from China and a generic version manufactured in Zimbabwe. Dr Verdoorn who has been investigating these cases for years says that most aldicarb is smuggled from Zimbabwe through our porous boarders one can easily cross the border on foot with a load of aldicarb and go unnoticed. It is also shipped in from China hidden in shipments and is then distributed nationally. It is an extremely organised crime syndicate, on one particular case when they tried to trace the addresses and names discovered on confiscated shipments all were fake and led to dead ends.
